values.label: Whole brain emulation
values.description: Scanning a brain and running it as software.

values.label: Brain computer interfaces
values.description: Devices that read from or write to the nervous system.

values.label: Neuromorphic AI
values.description: AI that borrows its architecture or learning rules from brains.

values.label: Hybrid
values.description: Proposals that combine more than one of the above.

values.label: Alignment
values.description: Getting advanced AI to reliably pursue what people actually want.

values.label: Intelligence Curse
values.description: AI eroding the economic and political value of human participation.

values.label: Both
values.description: Claims to address both alignment and the Intelligence Curse.

values.label: Possible
values.description: Reached once someone shows it can be done at all.

values.label: Widely available
values.description: Reached once it's reliable and affordable enough for lots of people to get.

values.label: Actually helping
values.description: Reached once it measurably helps with alignment or human agency.

values.label: Reliability and robustness
values.description: Works consistently outside the lab.

values.label: Technical capability
values.description: The technology can do the main thing it's meant to do.

values.label: Safety and welfare assurance
values.description: We can check that it's safe, including for any minds involved.

values.label: Scalable manufacture, compute or data
values.description: Can be produced or run at the scale needed.

values.label: Economic viability
values.description: Affordable enough that people will pay for it.

values.label: Legal and regulatory permission
values.description: Allowed by the relevant law and regulators.

values.label: Institutional capacity and public legitimacy
values.description: Institutions can run it and the public accepts it.

values.label: Equitable or broad access
values.description: Available beyond a small privileged group.

values.label: Not demonstrated
values.description: No one has shown this yet.

values.label: Prototype
values.description: Shown once, in limited conditions.

values.label: Replicated
values.description: Shown more than once, by more than one group.

values.label: Mature
values.description: Routine and dependable.

values.label: Not claimed
values.description: None of our current sources claims the proposal will do this.

values.label: High
values.description: Several relevant, reasonably solid sources support the judgment, and we've considered the main evidence against it.

values.label: Medium
values.description: Some relevant support, but with real limits.

values.label: Low
values.description: The judgment rests mainly on indirect evidence, early results or contested assumptions.

values.label: Strong
values.description: The mechanism is clear, relevant evidence supports it, and the main alternatives and ways it could fail have been substantially addressed.

values.label: Moderate
values.description: The mechanism is plausible and has some relevant support, but important assumptions or evidence gaps remain.

values.label: Weak
values.description: The mechanism doesn't target the outcome well, depends on especially demanding assumptions, or faces substantial evidence against it.

values.label: Unclear
values.description: We can't make a responsible call either way from the evidence available or the proposal as written. The reason is always given.

values.label: Not claimed
values.description: The proposal doesn't claim this outcome. This is different from Weak or Unclear.

values.label: High
values.description: The top of the scale.

values.label: Medium
values.description: The middle of the scale, judged on the same factors.

values.label: Low
values.description: The bottom of the scale. It needs evidence behind it and is never given just because nobody has studied a risk.

values.label: Unclear
values.description: We can't make a responsible call yet. The rating names its reason.

values.label: No relevant evidence found
values.description: We looked and found nothing relevant.

values.label: Conflicting evidence
values.description: Credible sources point in different directions.

values.label: Underspecified proposal
values.description: The proposal isn't specific enough to assess.

values.label: Search incomplete
values.description: We haven't finished looking.

values.label: Other
values.description: See the note.

values.label: Argument
values.description: Reasoning or analysis without new data.

values.label: Simulation
values.description: Results from a model or simulation.

values.label: Experiment
values.description: Results from a controlled study.

values.label: Deployment
values.description: Evidence from real-world use.

values.label: Review
values.description: A synthesis of other work.

values.label: Direct
values.description: About this exact scenario.

values.label: Adjacent
values.description: About a closely related scenario.

values.label: Remote
values.description: Only loosely related.

values.label: Independent
values.description: No stake in the outcome.

values.label: Non-biased
values.description: Some connection, but no obvious stake.

values.label: Affiliated
values.description: The author or funder has a stake in the outcome.

values.label: Peer reviewed
values.description: Published after peer review.

values.label: Preprint
values.description: Public but not yet peer reviewed.

values.label: Blog
values.description: A blog post or newsletter.

values.label: Report
values.description: A report from an organization.

values.label: Forum post
values.description: A post on a forum like LessWrong or the Alignment Forum.

values.label: Talk
values.description: A recorded talk or workshop presentation.

values.label: Podcast
values.description: A podcast episode or interview.

values.label: Book
values.description: A book or a chapter in one.

values.label: AI alignment
values.description: The source argues the approach could help align AI.

values.label: AI misalignment
values.description: The source argues the approach won't help with alignment, or could make misalignment worse.

values.label: Human empowerment
values.description: The source argues the approach could strengthen people's agency or bargaining power.

values.label: Human disempowerment
values.description: The source argues the approach could weaken people's agency, privacy or bargaining power.

values.label: Argument
values.description: Proposes or criticizes neuroengineering as a response to alignment or the Intelligence Curse.

values.label: Milestone evidence
values.description: Technical progress that bears on a milestone.

values.label: Core
values.description: Bears directly on a claim or milestone on this site.

values.label: Supporting
values.description: Backs up a core source or adds useful context.

values.label: Peripheral
values.description: Related background, rarely cited.

values.label: Not relevant
values.description: Unrelated to this project.

values.label: Strong
values.description: The methods are transparent, the claims match the evidence, and the work has been reviewed or replicated.

values.label: Adequate
values.description: Reasonable methods, with some gaps or overreach.

values.label: Weak
values.description: The methods are opaque, or the claims go well beyond the evidence.

values.label: Unclear
values.description: We can't judge it yet. The reason is given with the rating.

values.label: Near term
values.description: Definition to be agreed.

values.label: Medium term
values.description: Definition to be agreed.

values.label: Long term
values.description: Definition to be agreed.

values.label: From a source
values.description: Taken straight from a cited source, with the exact quote.

values.label: Our read
values.description: The team's own interpretation.

values.label: AI-suggested
values.description: Suggested by an AI model. The tag names the person who checked it, or says it hasn't been checked yet.

values.label: Unclear
values.description: We don't know, and the tag gives the reason.
